title: Read the document's units and object count
task: Read the active Rhino document's ModelUnitSystem and how many objects it holds (ObjectTable.Count), without changing anything. A read-only inspection of the document.
script:
# Task: read the active document's unit system and object count (read-only).
import scriptcontext as sc

# 1. ModelUnitSystem is an enum (Millimeters, Inches, ...); str() it for text.
units = str(sc.doc.ModelUnitSystem)

# 2. The object table's Count is every object in the model.
count = sc.doc.Objects.Count

result = "units=%s objects=%d" % (units, count)

pitfalls.symptom: Formatting ModelUnitSystem into a string with %s gives an enum member like 'Millimeters' that looks odd concatenated, or raises when used as a number.
pitfalls.cause: ModelUnitSystem is a Rhino.UnitSystem enum value, not a string or an int.
pitfalls.fix: Wrap it in str() before building the message; compare it against Rhino.UnitSystem members, never an integer.
